title: Do LLM routers actually route? Quick answer: not much
gist: Seven commercial and open routers in 17 settings, tested on 252 open-ended prompts against a pool of 20 models. None beat simply always calling a cheap strong model on quality and cost together, and several collapsed to sending nearly everything to one model.
changes: The counter-case for the model-choice lever. If a router cannot beat the cheap strong default, the lever reduces to picking that default well and revisiting it when models change.
caveats: Single-turn prompts with an LLM judge; agentic work is left for later. Several routers could reach only part of the pool. The author sells router benchmarking.

numbers.metric: Routers beating the cheap strong model on cost and quality together
numbers.baseline: always calling one cheap strong model

numbers.metric: Settings where one model received at least 90% of decisions

bears_on.note: Independent test: routing did not beat a fixed cheap model.
Vendors report 30 to 60% savings; an outside test finds none. Same lever, different rig.
